title: automated-onboard-priority-score-and-release-brief-generator
author: Maya Chopra
release_notes: Add automated onboarding priority score (onboard_score) and a concise release-brief generator that drafts one-line release notes and a short rationale for model version rollouts. Adds a CI validation step that ensures generated briefs meet length and privacy constraints.
body:
Motivation: Onboarding new models currently requires manual triage to decide rollout priority and to draft release notes. That slows curator velocity and leads to inconsistent brief quality. This PR introduces an automated onboard priority scorer (onboard_score) that combines telemetry signals, compatibility checks, and profile stability heuristics, plus a generator that drafts compact release brief snippets for changelogs and release announcements. What this change does (single-continuous description): Implements a lightweight heuristic-based scorer that combines the following signals: 1) observed production traffic similarity (sampled usage match), 2) profile stability (sigma of latency/throughput across probes), 3) evaluation quality delta on our curated prompt set, and 4) compatibility surface area (number of dependent consumers flagged via manifest). The score is normalized 0-100 and persisted as metadata field model.metadata.onboard_score.
Adds a brief generator that creates a 1-2 sentence release snippet and a 1-3 bullet micro-summary of expected impact (tokens, latency, recommended rollout windows). The generator keeps output under a 280-character headline plus a 3-line body by default and redacts any example prompts or customer-identifying telemetry. Implementation notes: - Registry schema migration: adds onboard_score and onboard_brief snapshot fields (backward compatible; absent for older models). - New CLI command: `redwood model suggest-onboard --model-id ` which returns the score and brief in JSON or plain text. - Background job: `onboard-scorer-worker` samples recent telemetry (bounded window, default 72h, max 1000 samples) and computes score; runs at configurable cadence (default daily). - Release brief CI hook: `validate-release-brief` runs against any generated brief, flagging length/privacy/style rule violations. - Unit tests: scorer logic, normalization, and redaction rules covered; e2e integration test for the CLI against a test fixture. - Perf guardrails: the worker uses reservoir sampling and early-exit heuristics to bound compute and memory. Files changed (high level): registry/db/migrations/20260218_add_onboard_columns.sql, registry/services/onboard_scorer.py, registry/services/brief_gen.py, cli/commands/suggest_onboard.py, ci/validate_release_brief.sh, tests/test_onboard_scorer.py, tests/test_brief_gen.py, docs/onboarding/auto-briefs.md, examples/onboard-sample.yaml and small updates to api/serializers.py and web/ui components to display the score in the model detail page. Security & privacy: The brief generator strips prompt examples and any PII-like fields. Telemetry sampling uses only aggregated/prod-metric-level signals; raw request text is never pulled into brief generation. The CI rule enforces that generated briefs pass a privacy redaction check. For private/on-prem customers the worker is disabled by default; CLI works offline with local telemetry if enabled. Testing and CI: Initial CI run failed lint (flake8/black) and one unit test related to sampling edge-cases. Fixed in follow-up commit `fix: sampling bound and lint` and re-ran CI. Final status: all checks passed. Migration/rollout plan: - Deploy schema migration with nullable fields. - Enable background worker in canary region for 48h with telemetry throttles. - Surface score in UI behind a feature flag. - After 2 weeks of telemetry, enable automatic brief suggestions in PR templates but keep human approval required for final release note publish. Why not ML model-based scoring: We intentionally used heuristic composition to avoid adding a new training lifecycle and to keep determinism and auditability for release audits. Future work: pluggable ML-based ranker behind the same API (ENG-5012). Related work: ENG-4938 (onboard automation), ENG-4721 (profile stability telemetry), PM-127 (release note UX).

bd2e44a implement basic onboard_scorer heuristic and tests

review_comments: Jared Klein: Good direction — please add a brief explainer of score composition and a reproducibility script so we can audit how a given score was derived.
Maya Chopra (author): Added a reproducibility endpoint `/api/v1/models/<id>/onboard_score/explain` that returns component contributions and sample counts (no raw text). See new serializer and tests.

Lina Morales: Need to ensure this is opt-in for Private customers; doc says disabled by default but please add a config flag and ensure worker doesn't attempt to call telemetry endpoints when disabled.
Maya Chopra: Added `ONBOARD_SCORER_ENABLED` param and guard checks in worker; unit tests assert worker no-op when disabled.
Aya Sato: CI hook looks fine but we should avoid failing PRs for minor style guidance — prefer warnings for suggested wording. Can we make length and privacy hard-fail but stylistic lint optional?
Maya Chopra: CI now enforces privacy and length as hard-fail; style suggestions are reported as warnings and surfaced in the PR comment. See `ci/validate_release_brief.sh` changes.
Lina Morales: Please add a small E2E job that runs the CLI suggestion against a representative model fixture to catch integration regressions.
Maya Chopra: Added `tests/e2e/test_cli_suggest_onboard.sh` which is run in the integration CI matrix.
Jared Klein: Approving after the fixes — nice work keeping this auditable and privacy-aware.
CI Bot: lint failed on bd2e44a, rerun after d4e2a11 -> all checks passed.
notes_for_changelog: Adds `onboard_score` metadata and an automated one-line brief generator for onboarding PRs; includes CLI, worker, CI validation, and docs. Briefs are opt-out for private installs and validated for privacy.
ui_display: score added to model detail page (hidden behind feature flag `ui.show_onboard_score`).
